Q: What algorithms are there for completing missing images? A:

This question is way too broad for SO. There are whole books on image repair and restoration algorithms and it remains an area of active research. Common heuristics are to fill gaps with something that is statistically plausible and matches the boundary conditions of the parts of the image that you do have.

Q: How to stream PostgreSQL (pgx.Rows) query results into a pager (less) without buffering the entire result set? A:

I don't believe it's possible to stream to more and less without buffering it all in.

From a query standpoint, running the queries with an order by, limit, and offset you can manually page things. It can run faster and use lest CPU,etc on the client side. It can get inefficient as well if you're reading the last page of a data set for example and it hasn't been ran recently (or cached). I do this all the time on web apps, but honestly, without modifying the code of the CLI, I'm not sure this would be easy without typing in specific "order by, limit, and offsets" every time you run the query.

Q: Database Design for quiz generation A:

First you need to decide how the quiz will work from an pattern standpoint.
Are questions going to be text only? Will they include images or any activities beyond just answering the question?

Will all answers be multiple choice? Any essay answers? Numeric answer? Anything else that'd be tricky? (math formulas where you'd have to type the pi symbol in, etc?

Once you get that figured out, it's a matter of putting the data in for those things. I can certainly give a full fledged answer, but we need to know what direction you're going with the actual questions and answers.
